purpose: Govern Industrial Library construction as a long-industrial civilization-memory shelf in original-era source form, inheriting Ancient/Medieval/Colonial seal discipline while accounting for modern rights and scale.

era_boundary.start_basis: post-Napoleonic settlement and consolidated industrial-imperial acceleration
era_boundary.end_basis: collapse of the Soviet Union and close of the Cold War world-order frame

internal_phases.description: restoration, liberalism, industrial capitalism, abolition, railways, print publics, nationalism, empire after revolution, and early socialist critique
high industrial empire, mass politics, global finance, professional science, labor organization, settler expansion, Meiji transformation, late Qing pressure, and imperial administrative thickening
world war, revolution, fascism, communism, depression, anti-colonial acceleration, total mobilization, genocide, and literary testimony of mass violence

decolonization, Cold War blocs, nuclear order, developmental states, human rights language, postcolonial literature, late socialism, neoliberal turn, media politics, and memory of industrial catastrophe

inherited_controls: separate roster-ready, metadata-ready, body-research-ready, admission-ready, seal-ready, and formally sealed
no source bodies in Git absent separately authorized governed override
online readability, catalogue presence, fame, citation density, or modern edition presence is not admission evidence
downloads, admissions, staging, commits, pushes, publication, and private Archive ingestion remain separately authorized
reviewable batches instead of one-authority loops
source-level and body-level coverage remain distinct
missing, restricted, needs-review, language, edition, survival, attribution, and rights debt remains explicit
literature is a primary civilization-memory witness
rights_and_edition_traps: post-1928 texts require source-specific rights posture
modern translations are distinct rights objects
government, party, speech, and international organization texts require source-specific rights review
newspapers, broadcasts, films, oral histories, and archival collections may have reuse limits despite online visibility
translated anti-colonial, Soviet, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Persian, African, and Latin American sources require edition and translator separation
corpus-heavy authorities must not be split artificially to cross body thresholds

batch_discipline.body_research_batch_authorities: 8-12 or fewer for severe rights/edition complexity
batch_discipline.hard_case_rule: Stop after one bounded source-recovery pass unless the operator explicitly authorizes deeper research.

acceptance_tests_before_roster_mutation: representation lanes and candidate functions named
Europe, war, and ideology do not dominate first draft
Indigenous, colonized, African, Asian, Latin American, Russian/Soviet, Islamic, and Atlantic/Pacific witnesses materially represented where source-feasible
rights traps identified before body research
each candidate classified no higher than evidence gate supports
first roster target and reserve logic explicit
